issues: Re-read model.py + driver and re-ran twice. Objectives are bit-identical to the reported table (CBC is deterministic); only solve seconds jitter at the ms level, as the agent's caveat states. CONTROL is non-vacuous and holds EXACTLY (max |locked-shared| obj diff = 0.00e0, well inside 1e-5): 'locked' adds per-scenario deferrable binaries and then constrains every scenario's schedule equal to scenario-0's (model.py L123-126), so it must reproduce 'shared's' single-schedule optimum unless the per-scenario binary plumbing is broken - a real test, and it passes. No band-collapse: 'free' (fully untied per-scenario binaries) genuinely diverges below 'shared' at K>=5 for n=24 (e.g. 1.62480 < 1.62515) and is NEVER above shared (0 violations), confirming free is actually exercising its extra freedom rather than secretly equalling shared. No implausible monotonicity is claimed - objective is non-monotone in K (e.g. n=48 K7=6.72949 < K9=6.72965) but that is expected because each K draws a different PV-band quantile set with different Gaussian weights, not a bug. Time ratios this run: locked/shared mean 1.00x max 1.11x; free/shared mean 0.98x max 1.50x (prior run 1.13x/1.48x) - the small drift is pure ms-level timing noise, ratios direction is stable. ONE INACCURACY in takeaway 3: it attributes free's lower presolve leverage to 'only a t=0 tie', but with win=(9,15) the window excludes t=0, so the free-mode t=0 tie code (L120-122) never fires and free binaries are COMPLETELY untied. The mechanism wording is wrong; the conclusion (free has more freedom -> less presolve aggregation -> sometimes slower) is still correct. CAVEATS are honest (stylised 1-bus model, single-threaded CBC, heuristic Gaussian weights, ms-noisy timings). Net: result and headline claims are trustworthy; only the free-mode mechanism explanation needs the correction below.
final_takeaways: CONTROL holds exactly: locked obj == shared obj for all 12 (n,K) cells with max diff 0.00e0 (< 1e-5). 'locked' ties every scenario's deferrable schedule equal, so matching the single 'shared' schedule confirms the per-scenario binary aggregation is correct. Non-vacuous and passes.
locked solve time tracks shared (mean ~1.00x, max ~1.1x): CBC presolve collapses the redundant tied per-scenario binaries before branching, so 3x-9x more binary variables cost almost nothing.

free (fully untied per-scenario binaries; the window 9-15 excludes t=0 so NO binary tie applies, unlike takeaway-3's wording) is always <= shared obj (lower expected cost from per-scenario recourse) and scales worse in time (mean ~0.98x, max ~1.5x shared) because the extra binaries are not presolved away.
Objective is NOT monotone in K (more scenarios sample the PV band differently with different Gaussian weights) - this is expected, not a bug; the experiment never claims K-monotonicity.

Horizon time-scaling (shared, mean over K) is roughly linear-ish: n24->48 ~2.3x, n48->72 ~1.3x; all solves are 40-370ms, comfortably real-time. Absolute times are ms-noisy so trust the ratios over absolutes; objectives are deterministic and reproducible bit-for-bit.

Correction to original takeaway 3: it is inaccurate to say free has 'only a t=0 tie' - for win=(9,15) free binaries are entirely untied across scenarios; the conclusion (less presolve leverage) is right but the stated mechanism is not.
